clue.text: Mission statement for today?

parts.note: the puzzle ran on 1 April, All Fools' Day, so a mission fitting the day is the pointless trip a prankster sends a dupe on

explanation.surface: A wry question about what today's company slogan should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mission statement' sounds like corporate jargon, but the paper was dated 1 April, April Fools' Day, and the mission is a pointless one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointless task that a joker sends someone on is exactly the kind of prank expected on April Fools' Day.

clue.text: Times of upheaval for endangered animal

indicators.note: an upheaval turns things upside down, so in this down clue the word of is read upwards

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Turbulent times threaten a creature already at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times of upheaval' looks like a phrase about troubled eras; in fact 'of' turned over by 'upheaval' gives FO, then X for 'Times'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox was a hunted quarry, an animal in danger from the hounds.

clue.text: Pair up to contain the French winger? Just about

indicators.note: means the turned word holds the French article inside
in this down clue the word for pair is read upwards

parts.note: two is a pair
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Two people team up to hold back a French wing player, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the pair word into OWT before 'to contain' takes the article in. 'Just about' is part of the definition: a fledgling owl can barely fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is only just becoming a flyer, so it is barely a winged creature yet.

clue.text: State capital's used for building in London

definitions.meaning: the capital city of Minnesota, with a possessive
Wren's cathedral in the City of London

explanation.surface: An American state capital's name is used for a London landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minnesota capital shares its name with Wren's cathedral, a famous London building.

clue.text: Horsed around with Scot from old colony

indicators.note: means the letters of horsed are moved round into a new order

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fooled about on horseback with someone from a former colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the British colony now Zimbabwe, and this adjective describes someone from there.

clue.text: It's straightforward, when split up

parts.note: the word meaning straight forward breaks into two words, an article and a body part

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a matter is simple once broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: Straight forward means onward; split it into A and a word for the top of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Going onward, in front, is going straight forward.

clue.text: Wilts about here — namely, kept in by germ, laid up

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for namely is held inside the turned germ
in this down clue the word for germ is laid upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a seed is a germ of new growth
viz is the abbreviation for videlicet, namely

explanation.surface: Someone wilts here, kept in bed and laid up with a germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' turns SEED into DEES. Wilts is short for Wiltshire, an English county; the clue reads like someone wilting while ill in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town lies in Wiltshire, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Vehicle used in police raid? Not last time

indicators.note: says the letter for time is dropped from the end of the word for the raid

parts.note: a bust is a police raid

explanation.surface: Wondering whether officers turned up for a raid in a van, though not the most recent one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Charming nature, to accept most of the blame

indicators.note: means the word for nature takes the shortened blame inside it

parts.note: a being is a nature or essence

indicators.note: means the last letter of the word for blame is dropped

parts.note: guilt is the blame for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone of charming disposition will shoulder most of the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting or delightful is charming.

clue.text: If not today, sometime in August?

definitions.text: If not today, sometime in August?

parts.words: If not today, sometime in August?
parts.note: the puzzle ran on April Fools' Day, a daft day; August is the quiet month of trivial news stories

explanation.surface: Someone postpones a date to the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle ran on 1 April. In Britain the late-summer slack season for news, mostly August, is known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: British papers call the August lull, when trivial stories fill the pages, by this name.

clue.text: One's struck by the Hammers' style of playing?

definitions.text: One's struck by the Hammers' style of playing?

parts.words: One's struck by the Hammers' style of playing?
parts.note: the Hammers suggests West Ham football club, but read literally an instrument played by striking bars with small hammers

explanation.surface: Someone is impressed by the way West Ham play football.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammers is the nickname of West Ham United, a London football club, so the clue seems to be about a fan admiring their play; really it is the mallets that strike a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument has wooden bars that are struck with beaters to sound notes.

clue.text: Wake during the night

parts.note: reads like stirring from sleep, but a wake is also a watch kept awake, often overnight

explanation.surface: Someone stirs from sleep in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch kept awake through the hours of darkness, as beside the dead or in prayer, is this.

clue.text: Gatecrash, being impolite after suggestion's ignored at first

indicators.note: places the word for impolite behind the shortened suggestion
means the opening letter of the word for suggestion is left out

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A party crasher is rude once nobody heeds the first hint to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter where one is unwelcome, which is to barge in uninvited.

clue.text: Amazingly, I'll figure out French oxymoron

definitions.text: Amazingly, I'll figure out French oxymoron

parts.words: Amazingly, I'll figure out French oxymoron
parts.note: a learning-impaired person with an astonishing gift such as calculating; the French term pairs fool with scholar, a contradiction

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they will crack a French contradiction in terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' looks like an anagram signal but there is no fodder: the speaker is a gifted calculator, and the French label pairs fool with learned man.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a mental disability yet a brilliant specific talent bears a French label meaning learned fool.

clue.text: Jazz trumpeter I left inside in dazed state

indicators.note: puts the I and the letter for left within the trumpeter's name

parts.note: Dizzy Gillespie was a famous jazz trumpeter

explanation.surface: A jazz trumpeter, left alone, wanders about in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something giddily, with the head spinning, is acting in a dazed state.

clue.text: Small bone some main customers picked

indicators.note: says only part of the run main customers is taken, the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A small bone has been picked out by some of the chief clients.
explanation.definitionFit: The anvil-shaped ossicle in the middle ear is one of the body's smallest bones.

clue.text: One's rolled up for food or mostly drink, after the game

indicators.note: places the shortened drink behind the game

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops

indicators.note: means the last letter of the word for drink is removed

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Something is rolled up to eat, or nearly all drunk once the match is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rolled cylinder of minced food coated in breadcrumbs and fried is rolled-up food.

clue.text: Unimpressed by one having huge piano imported

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: means the letter for piano is brought into the word for huge

parts.note: massive means huge
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone is unmoved by a person who has had an enormous piano shipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unmoved and showing no emotion is how an unimpressed person looks.

clue.text: Put out only hype about good history of evolution

indicators.note: means the rearranged letters go around the letter for good
means the letters of only hype are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by hype about good things only.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of how a species descended and branched over time is the evolutionary history of a group.

clue.text: After adjustments, net pay now almost worthless

indicators.note: means the letters of net pay now are reshuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Once deductions are taken, take-home pay is barely worth having.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so common it costs very little is of almost no value; the phrase is British for cheap and plentiful.

clue.text: Hurry up, discarding one character in picture about costly triumph

indicators.note: means the picture's word goes around the turned hurry

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: in this down clue the shortened hurry is read upwards
means the letter U is dropped from the word hurry

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A photographer urges speed, minus one person, in a shot about a dear victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarding one character' leaves HRRY, which 'up' turns to YRRH before 'about' puts the picture round it. Pyrrhus of Epirus won battles against Rome at ruinous cost.
explanation.definitionFit: King Pyrrhus beat Rome at such cost that a victory too dearly won is named after him.

clue.text: A new flood cut off part of Tayside

indicators.note: means the last letter of the word for flood is removed

parts.note: a gush is a flood or rush of liquid

explanation.surface: A fresh torrent isolates a district of eastern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Tayside was a Scottish region around the River Tay; Angus is a county within it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish county lay within the old Tayside region, on the east coast.

clue.text: Roman general with a firm hold on the borders of Parthia

parts.note: a grip is a firm hold

indicators.note: takes the first and last letters of Parthia

explanation.surface: A Roman commander keeps a tight hold on Parthia's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Parthia was an ancient empire east of Rome; Agrippa was Augustus's leading general.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a leading Roman commander under Augustus.

clue.text: Take food to fry in these containers?

definitions.text: Take food to fry in these containers?

parts.words: Take food to fry in these containers?
parts.note: fry suggests a frying pan, but fry are also baby fish, fed in fish tanks

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring food to cook in some vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' looks like cooking; here it means young fish, kept in tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tanks of water where fish, including tiny young ones, are kept and fed.

clue.text: Partly ring about raising capital

indicators.note: in this down clue the two pieces are lifted so they read upwards

parts.note: an arc is a part of a circle or ring
ca, circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A phone call made in part about raising capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: They can't face their opponents pulling ahead

definitions.text: They can't face their opponents pulling ahead

parts.words: They can't face their opponents pulling ahead
parts.note: sounds like timid rivals falling behind, but rowers sit facing backwards while pulling the boat forward

explanation.surface: Losing competitors cannot bear to watch their rivals take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers face the stern, so in a race they cannot see the crew they are pulling away from.

clue.text: City on East coast, one mile up a motorway

indicators.note: in this down clue the letters for one mile are read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A city on the east coast lies a mile up a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IM into MI. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: This Florida city lies on the Atlantic, the eastern seaboard of the USA.

clue.text: Briefly answer long letter

parts.note: A is the short form of answer
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Instructions to reply in short to a lengthy letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Man stocking fifth-rate standard?

parts.note: cheap describes goods of a low, inferior grade
Jack is a common name for any man

explanation.surface: A trader keeps goods of a very poor grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a flag; here it is the low quality of the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar of shoddy wares is a seller of poor-quality stock.

clue.text: Risk plunge, finally, over centre of Niagara, in a barrel

indicators.note: takes the last letters of risk and plunge
takes the middle letter of Niagara

explanation.surface: A daredevil takes the plunge over Niagara Falls in a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls daredevils who went over Niagara Falls in a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cask, as for beer, is a barrel.

clue.text: One in five usually going on foot

definitions.text: One in five usually going on foot

parts.words: One in five usually going on foot
parts.note: sounds like a walker among a group of five, but a foot normally has five digits

explanation.surface: A statistic that a fifth of people tend to walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit of the foot is one of the five a person normally has there.

clue.text: Flag's replacement may be what it's cracked up to be

definitions.text: Flag's replacement may be what it's cracked up to be

parts.words: Flag's replacement may be what it's cracked up to be
parts.note: a flag is a paving stone; a broken-up surface of irregular stones replaces flagstones and is literally cracked

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a new banner may live up to its reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is a flagstone; the idiom 'what it's cracked up to be' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A path made of irregular broken stones fitted together is laid instead of square flagstones.
